author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The New York Mets survived the loss of an eight-run lead and beat the Miami Marlins 15-14 on Wednesday night, completing a three-game road sweep in one of the season’s most volatile games.

New York led 8-0 in the third inning before Miami scored three times in the fourth and five in the sixth to tie the game. The Mets answered with six runs in the seventh, highlighted by Francisco Lindor’s three-run homer and Christopher Morel’s run-scoring single.

Morel finished 3-for-4 with three RBIs as the Mets extended their winning streak to four games. Miami continued to pressure the bullpen, but Tobias Myers recorded the final two outs for his second save and preserved the one-run margin.

The result improved New York’s run to 21-12 since the club sold at the trade deadline, according to Reuters. A 15-14 score can obscure how dramatically control shifted: the Mets built what appeared to be a comfortable advantage, surrendered all of it, then produced another major rally. The win mattered in the standings, but it also tested a reshaped roster’s ability to finish a game after momentum had fully reversed.
dek: New York recovered after Miami erased an 8-0 deficit, scoring six times in the seventh inning to complete a three-game sweep.
headline: Mets survive blown eight-run lead to beat Marlins 15-14
